title: Radish microgreen variety selection
subtitle: Which radish varieties to grow as microgreens, and what differs between them
excerpt: Most radish varieties work as microgreens, but four stand out for reliable germination, strong flavour, and visual impact. China Rose, Daikon, Sango, and Cherry Belle each produce a distinct cotyledon colour and flavour intensity, from mild pink-stemmed to vivid purple and sharply peppery.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens variety trials (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Radish microgreen variety comparisons synthesised from extension service material and established grower practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The seed leaf — the first leaf or pair of leaves produced by a germinating seed. In radish microgreens, the cotyledons are the harvested edible shoot. The colour and size of the cotyledons differs between radish varieties: from pale green through pink-stemmed to deep purple-red.

Buying seed specifically for microgreen growing requires checking for two things: that the seed is untreated (no fungicide coating), and that the variety is appropriate for microgreen use. Most standard vegetable varieties work as microgreens. Treated seed can cause poor germination and is unsuitable for food use at the microgreen stage.

content.text: Radish is one of the easiest microgreen crops to start with: fast, reliable, and available in enough variety to produce a range of colour and flavour. The four varieties below are the most widely grown for microgreens. All are sown and grown using the same method; the differences are in appearance and flavour intensity.

The most visually distinctive radish microgreen: pink to magenta stems with bright green cotyledons. Produces consistently colourful trays and a moderately peppery flavour. China Rose is the best choice when appearance on the plate matters. It is the variety most commonly sold by microgreen seed suppliers.

Daikon produces a microgreen with white or pale green stems and medium green cotyledons. The flavour is slightly stronger and sharper than China Rose: the peppery heat comes through more clearly. Daikon microgreens are a good choice for dishes where flavour intensity matters more than stem colour. Germination is fast and reliable.

Sango is a purple-leafed radish that produces cotyledons with deep red-purple stems and seed leaves. The visual impact on the plate is the highest of any radish variety. The flavour is mild compared to China Rose or Daikon: slightly less peppery and more delicate. The deep colour comes from anthocyanins, which develop fully in bright light.

Cherry Belle is a standard red radish that gives green-stemmed microgreens with a mild peppery flavour. It germinates quickly and is the most widely available in general vegetable seed ranges. A good starting point before buying specialist microgreen seed.

: all four varieties are available from microgreen seed suppliers in packs sized for home tray growing (100 g to 500 g). Microgreen suppliers label seed as untreated; standard vegetable seed from garden centres should also be checked for treatment status on the packet.
colour is the main difference between varieties at the microgreen stage. The sowing method, blackout time, light needs, and harvest timing are the same for all four.
